answer: Resist sybils with coin-age weighting: an identity's influence grows only from coins it has held untouched in one address for many epochs, like a jade stone gaining value in a quiet haven. Splitting one pot across a thousand clones divides the coin-days, so the farm's total weight never grows; a raven flying solo with aged coins outweighs the whole flock. An attacker must lock fresh capital for a long time per clone, paying real opportunity cost.
